clue.text: Mad scottie that's mangled little boy needs to be this?

definitions.text: Mad scottie that's mangled little boy needs to be this?

indicators.note: something mangled is torn about and misshapen, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: Ed is a short boy's name, a little form of Edward

explanation.surface: A dog that has savaged a small child clearly needs taming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangled' shuffles the two words into DOMESTICAT. The whole clue is also the definition: a mad dog that has savaged a child needs taming.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious dog must be tamed and house-trained, made fit to live with people.

clue.text: Progresses after poor exam grades in mocks

indicators.note: after says the word for progresses comes behind the grades

parts.note: D and E are low marks in an exam
rides means moves along, progresses

explanation.surface: A student's progress report notes weak exam results in the practice papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mocks' looks like the noun for practice exams, fitting the exam surface; it is the verb meaning ridicules.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to ridicule or scorn them, a synonym of mocks as a verb.

clue.text: Indicates financial resources available

explanation.surface: A report signals how much money is on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean is to signify or indicate; a person's means are the money and wealth they have to spend.

clue.text: Trembling in silence, I'm engaged?

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
an engaged person can say I've (got a) ring, so the phrase is read as I'VE RING

explanation.surface: A nervous newly engaged person quivers with emotion in a hushed room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm engaged' is read cryptically: someone engaged can say I'VE (a) RING. The 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivering is shaking or quivering, as with cold or nerves.

clue.text: One acquiring old books and a letter

indicators.note: acquiring says the first piece takes on the others, which join it at its back

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone buys antique volumes and a piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence after 'books', but here it is a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Any crest may show the family line

indicators.note: may show suggests the letters of these words can display something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat of arms reveals a family's lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may show' rearranges ANY CREST; the surface about heraldic crests fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's descent, the line of forebears stretching back through generations.

clue.text: Kick out old flame quietly (Ethel completely gutted)

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters of the name Ethel

explanation.surface: Ethel, utterly devastated, quietly throws out a former lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely gutted' sounds like Ethel is devastated; it strips her name to its first and last letters, E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force out or eject, as from a school or club.

clue.text: A Laotian relocated in Asian peninsula

indicators.note: relocated says the letters of these words are moved into new places

explanation.surface: Someone from Laos has moved to live in a region of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' rearranges A LAOTIAN; 'in' is a link. Anatolia is the peninsula forming most of Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia, or Asia Minor, is the large peninsula between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Criminal appears and is caught in short time

indicators.note: is caught in says the word and is held inside another piece

parts.note: a bit is a short while, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: A crook turns up and is arrested soon after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link; 'and' itself is the word caught in BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Practical part of chore — a list I constructed

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone drew up a to-do list, a sensible approach to housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means sensible and practical, facing things as they are.

clue.text: Badmouth daughter wanting a beast unsuitable as pet!

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a daughter for wanting an inappropriate animal as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link here, not a deletion signal. The panda is a large wild bear from China.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a large, endangered wild bear, hardly a household companion.

clue.text: Destroyed hut with girl at front of it

indicators.note: at front of it puts the girl's name before the word for hut

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: A girl stands in front of a ruined hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyed' looks like it describes the hut; it is the definition, in the sense of dashed hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dished is an informal word for ruined, as in hopes dished by defeat.

clue.text: One criticised about nothing becomes cut off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about says the word for criticised wraps around the nothing

parts.note: slated means harshly criticised
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone attacked over nothing ends up isolated from friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means remote and separated from others, alone.

clue.text: Return journeys — one's collected gin maybe

indicators.note: the journeys word has collected the one, holding it inside
return says the word for journeys is read backwards

parts.note: trips are journeys
I is the Roman numeral for one; one's means one has

explanation.surface: On the way home from trips, someone has picked up a bottle of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, which collects I (one) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is an example of a distilled alcoholic drink, a liquor.

clue.text: Business arrangement is sealed by Italian who won't compromise?

indicators.note: sealed by says the Italian piece closes around the others like a seal

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
a deal is a business arrangement

explanation.surface: An Italian negotiator closes a business deal and refuses to give ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealed' suggests clinching a business deal, but here 'sealed by' means closed inside the Italian abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist holds to high principles and refuses to settle for less.

clue.text: Couple allowed to join band

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Two people are permitted to join a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group; it is a band worn round the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Alliances of companies contrived actions to secure gold

indicators.note: to secure suggests holding something inside, enclosing it
contrived says the letters of actions are artfully rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Business cartels take contrived measures to hold on to their gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges the word actions into CONSTIA, which 'to secure' then wraps around the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are groupings of firms or organisations formed for a joint venture.

clue.text: Shampoo and what may follow to get one looking tidy?

parts.note: to shampoo is to clean hair
after a shampoo at the hairdresser a haircut often follows

explanation.surface: A hair wash followed by a trim makes someone look neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut describes a neat, wholesome appearance.

clue.text: Girl attracted to football manager, one who was bad influence

indicators.note: attracted to says the girl is drawn up against the manager, placed next to him

parts.note: Sven-Goran Eriksson was a well-known football manager, including of England
a gal is a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl falls for a football manager who led her astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Sven-Goran Eriksson managed England's football team; tabloids covered his love life. Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: A Svengali is a person who manipulates and controls another, after the sinister hypnotist in Trilby.

clue.text: District with soldiers undermining religious group

indicators.note: in a down clue, undermining puts the soldiers below the religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops subvert a religious faction in a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermining' suggests subversion; in a down answer it simply places OR under SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct area or zone, as in a military or city sector.

clue.text: Like a glove in one's possession?

explanation.surface: A question about having something to hand, framed as a glove.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove is worn over a hand; something available or ready at hand is held by you.

clue.text: Heads of department expect set of principles to be laid down

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs or principles

explanation.surface: Department heads anticipate that principles will be established.
explanation.definitionFit: Decreed means officially ordered, as rules are set down by authority.

clue.text: Chart shows gangster facing death in vehicle

indicators.note: in says the gangster and death go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: facing puts the gangster in front of the word for death

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
end means death

explanation.surface: A diagram depicts a gangster meeting his end in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, the Chicago gangster; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a chart or table of the days, weeks and months of a year.

clue.text: Egg about to be served with salt

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An egg is about to be served with salt at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' and 'salt' suggest breakfast; a nit is a louse egg and nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is saltpetre, potassium nitrate, a chemical salt.

clue.text: Pattern of law in the ot

explanation.surface: A pattern of religious law in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ot' is the Old Testament; the law of Moses is set out there.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a design made of small tiles; Mosaic also means relating to Moses, the lawgiver.

clue.text: Active soldier imbibes alcohol? On the contrary

indicators.note: imbibes says one piece drinks in the other, holding it inside
on the contrary reverses the roles, so the drink takes in the soldier instead

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A lively soldier drinks some alcohol, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the clue: the drink takes in the soldier, not the soldier the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving, physically lively.

clue.text: One opposing artificial aid to worship?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
con means against, opposing, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone objects to artificial devices used in worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' is a link, hinting that an icon is a made image. Icons are painted images venerated in Orthodox churches.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious image used as a focus for prayer and devotion.

clue.text: Number retreating then decide on attack

indicators.note: retreating says the abbreviation for number goes backwards

parts.note: to set is to fix or decide on, as a date

explanation.surface: Troops retreat and then resolve to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or the start of an attack.

clue.text: Commander taking a moment — indication of old wound

indicators.note: taking says the commander is followed by the rest, which join it

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
a trice is an instant, a moment

explanation.surface: A commander pauses over a scar from an old injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicatrice is a scar, the healed mark left by a wound.

clue.text: Gaining ground in finding a principal for school

parts.note: getting means obtaining or finding
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: Someone advances by finding a new headteacher for a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting ahead means making progress or advancing in life.
